Definition: from G1909 and G321; to lead up on, i.e. (technical) to put out (to sea); (intransitively) to return:--launch (thrust) out, return.
BiblicalUsage: To put out to sea, or to return. Jesus tells Simon to launch out into the deep in Luke 5:4, after teaching from his boat a little way from land in Luke 5:3, and in the morning He returned into the city and hungered in Matthew 21:18.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe 'launch out' is still the Lord's word to me — the deep is where the draught is, and the shallow water never caught anything. I hold that the same Lord who went back into the city hungry is the Lord who fills the nets when I obey Him.
